verdicts.rationale: The divergence hint is the Charged-Attack consuming the Lightning Stiletto to fire additional Electro hits (Thunderclap Slash). These are Keqing's own on-field damage instances — damage numbers/math and a damage-proc render surface, both constitution-excluded and un-implementable in this pass. The CA still renders as a CA; there is no rendered surface that diverges (no damage-instance lane). The residual — that a CA can consume the stiletto as an alternative to the E recast — is framed by the note itself as an open curator authoring decision ('reviewer to decide if a conditional chargeFrames variant or a skill effect is more appropriate'), is an edge case requiring the user to notate a CA inside the recast window, and does not clear the skeptical purpose-test bar. Default to noCaveat.
rubricRefs: Out of scope by constitution: damage numbers/math
Curator reasoning, sources, frame numbers, schema/field talk -> _curatorNotes

groundedIn.claim: The unmodeled behavior is a CA producing 2 additional Electro damage hits (self on-field), left as an open curator authoring decision.
groundedIn.quote: Thunderclap Slash: CA while Lightning Stiletto is active fires 2 additional Electro hits at the stiletto location (skillCA scaling, 2× hits, per charge.go). Not modeled in chargeFrames — reviewer to decide if a conditional chargeFrames variant or a skill effect is more appropriate.

groundedIn.claim: The Charged Attack itself is a plain rendered normal-side action, so there is no separate divergent surface for the extra hits.
groundedIn.quote:
Charged Attack
Consumes a certain amount of Stamina to unleash 2 rapid sword strikes.

verdicts.rationale: The lone divergence hint is a curator cross-reference: the Charged-Attack consumption of the Stiletto is explicitly filed as a normal-side mechanic documented elsewhere, not a skill-side omission. This is curator process-talk about where a mechanic is (or isn't) authored, which belongs in _curatorNotes, not a user-facing caveat. The skill itself models what it should — the E-recast chain is authored via chainStage (index 0 opening the 5.33s Stiletto window, the recast as a reachable second-E). Nothing on the skill's rendered timeline diverges. Default to noCaveat.
rubricRefs: Curator reasoning, sources, frame numbers, schema/field talk -> _curatorNotes

groundedIn.claim: The skill-side note is a cross-reference stating the CA-consume mechanic lives on the normal ability, not that the skill omits something user-facing.
groundedIn.quote: Charged-Attack consumption of the Stiletto (the alternate to the E recast) is a normal-side mechanic, not modeled here.

groundedIn.claim: The E-recast chain the skill is responsible for is already modeled via chainStage, so the skill's rendered behavior is not diverging.
groundedIn.quote: Authored as chainStage index 0 with window 5.33 — a second E within the window resolves to the recast (keqing__skill__stellar_restoration_recast), mirroring Diluc's E1/E2/E3 chainStage pattern.

verdicts.rationale: C2 produces an Elemental Particle on Normal/Charged hits against Electro-affected enemies. Particle/energy generation is explicitly out of scope by the tool constitution, so it is neither caveat-worthy nor implementable. No effect is authored (no render surface to diverge from), and the note documents a legitimate deferral: the 50%-chance gate is un-expressible and the effect itself is energy/particle generation. This is constitution-excluded on two counts. Default to noCaveat.
rubricRefs: Out of scope by constitution: ... orb/particle collection

groundedIn.claim: The C2 mechanic is Elemental Particle generation, which is energy/particle-domain and out of scope.
groundedIn.quote:
When Keqing's Normal and Charged Attacks hit opponents affected by Electro, they have a 50% chance of producing an Elemental Particle.
This effect can only occur once every 5s.

groundedIn.claim: No effect is authored and the deferral is documented, so there is no rendered surface diverging.
groundedIn.quote: Defer authoring: the 50%-chance gate is not expressible in the schema (no probabilistic-trigger primitive), and authoring without it would make the buff over-render at 100% rate vs the in-game 50%.
